tagline: Complex AI. Explained visually. Built practically.
title: Why AI Sometimes Hallucinates
disclosure: Fictional teaching scenario. Wouri Express and its people are invented; the setting draws on documented conditions in Douala, Cameroon.

onScreen.text: The report said a truck broke down on the Bonabéri road.
onScreen.emphasis: No truck broke down. No driver wrote it. The AI made it up.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: The week thirty-nine report said a truck broke down on the Bonabéri road. Mbella called the mechanic. No truck had broken down.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: No driver wrote it. The AI made it up, fluently, with confidence. That is a hallucination. Here is why it happens.

onScreen.title: Why AI Sometimes Hallucinates
onScreen.subtitle: AI Fundamentals · Lesson 9 · The breakdown that never happened at Wouri Express, Douala

messages.text: Mbella: If one sentence in the report can be invented, how do I trust the other twenty?
Mbella: I do not want it to stop. I want to know which sentences are real.

ui.title: Ndedi's check
lines: Report: “truck breakdown on the Bonabéri road”
The gap was filled with a plausible story

lines.speaker: amara
lines.text: Mbella's question is fair, Tanyi. If one sentence can be invented, how does she trust the other twenty? Which ones are real?

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Ndedi found the gap. The driver wrote late, sorry. The model filled it with a plausible story. Understanding why is the first fix.

scenes.label: Understand: where the story comes from

onScreen.title: How a gap becomes a confident sentence

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: The model predicts the most likely next words. In the text it learned from, a late delivery is often followed by a reason. Breakdown is common.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: When message eighty-eight has a gap, the model fills it with what usually goes there. Completing a pattern, not reporting a fact.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Reason not stated is rare in ordinary text, so it rarely comes out on its own. You have to make it allowed, and expected.

left.title: Before
items: No way to check a claim

right.title: After
items: Numbers pasted by code, not written

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Three changes. Every cause must cite a message number. Not stated is a valid answer, written into the instruction. Numbers come from code.

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: And one rule for people. Any claim about a driver, a customer or money is checked against its source before it leaves the building.

items.text: For every cause, cite the message numbers
If no message states a cause, write: reason not stated
Never add a cause that is not in a message

messages.text: Delivery 88: late, reason not stated (message 88). Four deliveries this week have no stated reason.

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: The instruction now says: cite a message for every cause. If no message states one, write reason not stated. Those exact words.

lines.speaker: amara
lines.text: And then ordinary code checks each citation? So a cause with no real message behind it is rejected before anyone reads it.

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: Exactly. Breakdown had no message, so it was rejected. Delivery eighty-eight now reads: late, reason not stated. Four this week.

onScreen.title: A hallucination with a fake source

steps.title: It cites a message that says something else

messages.text: Customer absent at the pharmacy, source: message 27.

steps.title: Kito reads message 27
steps.detail: The source does not support the claim

ui.title: Message 27
lines: Citation exists, claim does not match

items.text: Quote the words from the message next to the cause
Code checks the quote appears in that message
Ndedi spot-checks five claims every week

lines.speaker: hallucinator
lines.text: Customer absent at the pharmacy. Source: message twenty-seven. See, I cite my sources now. Fully reliable.

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: Message twenty-seven says port gate queue again, two hours. Nothing about a pharmacy. A citation is not proof. I require the quote.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: A model can hallucinate a source as easily as a fact. So: quote the words, code checks the quote, and a person spot-checks five claims a week.

steps.title: Every claim carries its words
steps.detail: She can check any line in seconds

messages.text: Floods, 6 late. Message 19: “Road at Bonabéri flooded. Turning back.” Message 33: “Water on the road at Bonabéri.”
Mbella: Now I can trust the other twenty.

ui.title: Send week 40 report? 5 claims spot-checked by Ndedi.

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: Week forty. Every cause carries the driver's own words. Mbella can check any line in seconds.

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: Ndedi spot-checked five claims. Only then does it go out. Trust is built by checking, not by hoping.

items.label: Law office
items.text: Every cited case must be quoted and found

items.label: Clinic
items.text: Dosages come from the formulary, never from the model

items.label: Finance
items.text: Figures pasted from the ledger, sentences drafted around them

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Higher stakes, same fix. A law office quotes and finds every cited case. A clinic takes dosages from the formulary. Finance pastes figures from the ledger.

onScreen.title: Who owns this?
items: The citation check is company code, not a model promise
Ndedi's weekly spot-check is part of her job
A wrong claim that goes out is the company's error

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: The citation check is company code, not a model's promise. Ndedi's weekly spot-check is her job. A wrong claim that goes out is the company's error.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: AI hallucinates because it completes patterns, and a fluent guess is more likely than an honest gap. Allow the gap, demand the quote, check with code.

onScreen.title: Your build challenge
items: Add one line to your next prompt:

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Your challenge: add one line to your next prompt. Quote your source for every claim, and if there is none, say so.
